arcs.title: Dana: Haifa
arcs.stage: Fri: 18:30 at Avi's fixed; the 04 number face down. Sat Nov 21: the first date: falafel at Avi's, eleven sorries counted, the park, she starts 'if someone offered you...' and the 04 number cuts in; The Island of Doctor Moreau; at his door: 'Wednesday. I'll tell you Wednesday.' Next: midpoint Wed Nov 25, Lior lets it slip before she can.
arcs.secret: Dana has been offered a job running a new cafe in Haifa from January and must answer by Mon Dec 7. She has not told Ishai.

arcs.title: Gadi: Unpaid
arcs.stage: Fri: the Shabbat 'tiny thing', Ishai: 'Sunday. Nothing else.'; then Gadi phoned at night all cheer, 'Sunday, promise'. Next: Sunday's number; Ruti still unanswered.
arcs.secret: Sababa Creative lost its biggest client in October. Gadi is paying every freelancer late and hides it behind cheerful 'small things'.

arcs.title: Noa: Shir
arcs.stage: Fri: Shabbat with Ishai; 'Shir' during the blessing; red eyes on the stairs, 'plumbers, the landlord, whatever'; the armchair. Sat: goes home in the morning ('I'm becoming furniture'), slips 'no excuse' for 'no reason'; asks if he'd open a box someone left. Tomer has called her twice. Next: Sat Nov 28 he finds out.
arcs.secret: Noa's girlfriend of three years, Shir, moved out in October. Noa told nobody: it's why she is late, cancels plans and pushes Ishai's love life so hard.

arcs.title: Improv on Thursdays
arcs.stage: Lesson 3 Thu Nov 19: the toaster refund; 'I want to be paid for what I already did'. Yael let slip Noa paid cash. Homework (a no to someone he likes) used on Noa's plumbers, then on Gadi's Shabbat 'tiny thing'. Lesson 4 Thu Nov 26, the last one Noa paid for.

arcs.title: Mrs. Levi's cough
arcs.stage: Fri: Moti's chicken; the video call 'not yet'. Sat after havdalah: Ishai fixes her phone's camera and sees Eli's last video call: March 2022. She won't call: 'Toronto is busy.' Next: week 3, Ishai quietly messages Eli.
arcs.secret: Mrs. Levi is lonely: her son Eli in Toronto hasn't visited in four years, and she always says he's busy.

arcs.title: Avi's kiosk
arcs.stage: Tue: no proverb, a lawyer's envelope. Thu: 'the proverbs are finished, I have a calculator'; 'Gadi is a cloud'. Next: Ishai asks properly (week 3); the first date starts at his kiosk Saturday.
arcs.secret: Avi's landlord is doubling the kiosk's rent from January.

arcs.title: Lior's novel and Moshe
arcs.stage: Wed: chapter thirteen, the coat for a cold city; 'up north'. Fri: chapter fourteen, 'the barista practises the names of streets she has never walked'; asks Ishai if he knows streets up north. Ishai still doesn't recognise himself ('the man in your book sounds like a pushover').
arcs.secret: Lior's novel is about Ishai: 'the man who apologises to his coffee'.

arcs.title: Tomer and Noa
arcs.stage: Thu: fifty-shekel bet that Dana moves to Eilat. Fri: at the bar, 'Noa sounded weird'. Sat: texts Ishai 'for science' advice; has called Noa twice, she says 'Tomer says everybody sounds weird'. Next: showing up for Noa.
arcs.secret: Tomer has liked Noa since school.

arcs.title: Mr. Zelig's bench
arcs.stage: Sat Nov 21: the morning of the date. Mr. Zelig: 'listen to what she doesn't say'; 1971 again; Tomer's text ('ask her where she sees herself in a year') overruled: 'ask where she is tonight'.

arcs.title: The poker table
arcs.stage: Thu Nov 19: Boaz invited Ishai at Avi's (50 to buy in, small notes, don't touch Yossi's cap); Fri: Moti 'counts the pizza slices'. First night Mon Nov 23 (engine). After it: Yossi asks Ishai to lend him 200.
arcs.secret: Yossi is broke: the lucky cap hasn't paid in months, and he owes money at the depot.

beats.goal: Saturday morning after Noa's third night on the armchair. She has folded the good blanket too neatly and is dressed to leave. Over coffee she coaches him one last time for tonight's date (one question, no sorry), then says she's going home: 'the plumbers finished, I have no excuse' and corrects it to 'no reason'. She asks him, as if about a film, whether he would open a box someone left behind. Tomer has called her twice; 'Tomer says everybody sounds weird.' Ishai keeps his no-questions promise, but offers the armchair any time. She goes.
beats.teaser: Noa folds the good blanket. Is she really going home?
beats.forceText: Noa folds the blanket, coaches him for the date over coffee and goes home, saying the plumbers are done.

forceLines.say: One question. No sorry. And the jacket, not the hoodie.

forceCommentary.say: She folded that blanket like she was leaving a hotel she loved.
'No excuse.' Then 'no reason.' Write that down.

moments.text: Morning light. The good blanket is folded in a perfect square on the armchair. Noa, coat already on, drinks coffee at the counter while Ishai feeds Falafel.

lines.say: Rise and shine, lover boy. Today's the day.
It's ten. And Shabbat. Talk quieter.
Rule one. Ask her one real question.
I know rule one. You said it nine times.
Rule two. Count your sorries. Over five, you go home.
Over five I'll be home anyway. Hiding.
And the jacket. Not the hoodie.
The hoodie is lucky.
The hoodie has soup on it.
You folded the blanket. You never fold.
I'm a guest. Guests fold.
Three nights. You're more like a tenant.
Exactly. I'm becoming furniture.
Good furniture. Moshe likes you.
Moshe likes anyone who doesn't water him.

commentary.say: Rule two: count your sorries. Somebody get the man an abacus.
Coat on at ten on Shabbat. Noa is leaving like it's an escape plan.

moments.text: Noa rinses her cup, picks up her duffel by the door, then stops with her hand on the handle and turns around.

lines.say: Okay. I'm going home. The plumbers finished, I have no excuse.
Excuse?
Reason. No reason. Same thing.
Okay.
Can I ask you something? Like, about a film.
Is it a horror film? I'm seeing one tonight.
Someone leaves a box of their things behind. Do you open it?
Whose things?
It's a film, Ishush. Characters.
Then... no. I'd keep it closed until they asked.
Even if they never ask?
Then it's a very long film.
Tomer called me twice. Says I sounded weird.
He said that to me too.
Tomer says everybody sounds weird.
The armchair's here. Any time. No questions.
I know. Go get your barista.

commentary.say: 'It's a film, Ishush.' Sure. And I'm a weather girl.
No excuse, then no reason. That correction did a lot of work.

update.memory: Left his armchair after three nights, said the plumbers finished. Asked about the box 'like a film'. He kept his promise. Tomer keeps calling.

beats.goal: Shabbat midday walk with Falafel in the park. Mr. Zelig is on his bench feeding the pigeons. Ishai, nervous about tonight, sits down. Zelig reminds him Dana sat on this bench on Thursday looking at her phone 'like it was the sea'. A text from Tomer: 'fifty says Eilat; ask her where she sees herself in a year, for science'. Zelig overrules it: don't ask where she'll be in a year, ask where she is tonight, and listen to what she doesn't say. 1971: 'I stayed.'
beats.teaser: Mr. Zelig gives Ishai first-date advice. The pigeons disagree.
beats.forceText: In the park Mr. Zelig tells Ishai to listen to what Dana doesn't say tonight; Tomer texts bad advice.

forceLines.say: Don't ask where she'll be in a year. Ask where she is tonight.

forceCommentary.say: A man who talks to pigeons just out-coached Noa.
Listen to what she doesn't say. Chills. Actual chills.

moments.text: Quiet Shabbat noon in the park. Mr. Zelig sits on his bench throwing crumbs to the pigeons. Ishai sits at the other end with Falafel, who watches the pigeons very seriously.

lines.say: The dog wants the pigeons. The pigeons want the bread. Nobody wants me.
Shabbat shalom, Mr. Zelig.
You have a face like a man with an appointment.
Tonight. A first date.
The barista. With the leaves on the coffee.
How do you know that?
She sat here Thursday. Right where you are.
Here? Alone?
With her phone. She looked at it like it was the sea.
Which sea?
Not this one. I told you. Not this sea.
That doesn't help, Mr. Zelig.
It isn't help. It's information.
Sorry. I mean, thank you.
Ha. You say sorry to old men and pigeons.

commentary.say: Dana. On this bench. Staring at her phone like a sea. Hello?!
Falafel versus the pigeons. Nobody's moved. It's chess.

moments.text: Ishai's phone buzzes; he reads a text from Tomer out loud. Mr. Zelig shakes his head and throws the last crumbs.

message.say: Fifty says Eilat. Ask her where she sees herself in a year. For science. Don't say sorry.

lines.say: Tomer says ask her where she sees herself in a year.
No. That's a question for a bank.
Then what do I ask?
Ask where she is tonight. Only tonight.
She'll be at the cinema. With me.
No, boy. Where she is. Inside.
And if she doesn't answer?
Then listen to what she doesn't say.
Did you do that? In 1971?
In 1971 a girl had a ticket to somewhere.
And?
And I stayed. I told you. I stayed.
That's not the end of the story.
It's the end I have. Go. Your dog is bored.
Thank you, Mr. Zelig. Really.

commentary.say: 'That's a question for a bank.' Zelig, killing Tomer's career in dating.
A girl with a ticket to somewhere. Why is everyone talking about leaving today?

update.memory: Told Ishai before his date: ask where she is tonight, listen to what she doesn't say. Told him again: in 1971 I stayed.

beats.goal: Right after havdalah, as Ishai comes out dressed for the date, Mrs. Levi (scarf, still coughing) is waiting on the landing with her phone: the camera 'faces the wrong way' and Moti never came. Ishai fixes it in a minute. Opening the video calls he sees Eli (Toronto) in her favourites: the last video call was March 2022. He offers to call now; she refuses ('Toronto is busy; you have a barista'), fixes his collar and sends him off. He goes down the stairs thinking about it.
beats.teaser: Mrs. Levi's phone camera faces the wrong way. So does something else.
beats.forceText: On the landing Ishai fixes Mrs. Levi's phone camera and sees Eli's last video call was in 2022. She sends him off to his date.

forceLines.say: Toronto is busy. Go, your barista is waiting.

forceCommentary.say: March 2022. That number hit harder than the horror film will.
He fixed the camera. The camera wasn't the problem.

moments.text: Shabbat is out. Ishai locks his door in his good jacket. Mrs. Levi is waiting on the landing in a thick scarf, holding her phone out at arm's length like it bit her.

lines.say: Shavua tov. Look at you. A jacket.
Shavua tov, Mrs. Levi. How's the cough?
Bored of me. Ishai, the camera. It shows my ceiling.
Moti said he'd come after Shabbat.
Moti said. Moti also said the stair light.
Give it. It's just flipped. Front camera...
Front, back. In my day a phone had one face.
There. Now it shows you.
Oy. Now it shows me. Turn it back.
It's a video call, it has to show you.
Then I need lipstick first.
Who are you calling?
Nobody. In case. In case someone calls.
Let me check it works. Video calls...
Careful. Don't press anything brave.

commentary.say: 'Moti also said the stair light.' The committee's credibility, destroyed in one line.
Lipstick for a call that hasn't happened. Mrs. Levi, I'm not okay.

moments.text: Ishai opens her video calls. At the top of the list: 'Eli Toronto ❤'. Under it, the date of the last call: March 2022. He looks at it a second too long; she takes the phone back.

lines.say: Eli. Last video call... March 2022.
Give me that.
Do you want me to call him? Now? It works now.
Now? It's night in Toronto.
It's eleven in the morning in Toronto.
Then he's at work. Toronto is busy.
Saturday morning?
Ishai. You're late for a girl.
Twenty minutes early, actually.
Then you're early for a girl. Worse. Come here.
What?
Your collar. A man with a crooked collar says sorry all night.
I'm sorry. I mean, thank you.
See? Already. Go. Bring me the story tomorrow.
With the cats' breakfast. Promise.

commentary.say: March 2022. She keeps a heart next to his name and a lock on the button.
Sorry number one of the night. And he hasn't even left the building.

update.memory: Ishai fixed my phone camera before his date and saw Eli's last call. Wanted to call him. I said Toronto is busy. I fixed his collar.

beats.goal: The first date begins at 18:30 at Avi's falafel kiosk on Herzl Street, as fixed. Dana arrives in a coat, not her apron; Ishai is early and has already apologised to the bench. They eat falafel standing at the counter; Avi is watching (no proverbs lately) and slips them extra pickles. Ishai keeps saying sorry and Dana starts counting out loud. He asks one real question (Noa's rule). Warm, awkward, funny. Then they walk toward the park.
beats.teaser: Ishai and Dana's first date, at Avi's falafel kiosk. Counting sorries.
beats.forceText: Dana meets Ishai at Avi's kiosk for their first date; she counts his sorries while they eat falafel.

forceLines.say: That's four sorries. It's eighteen thirty-five.

forceCommentary.say: Four sorries in five minutes. On pace for a record.
She's COUNTING. That's flirting, Ishai. That's flirting!

moments.text: Evening on Herzl Street, Shabbat just out, the kiosk's light on. Ishai stands by Avi's counter in his good jacket. Dana walks up in a long coat, no apron, hair down.

lines.say: You're early.
Sorry. I mean, hi. You look... no apron.
I own other clothes. It's a shock, I know.
Sorry. That came out weird.
That's two.
Two what?
Sorries. I'm counting. Noa told me to.
Noa talked to you?
She came for coffee. Said 'count them'. Very serious.
That's a betrayal.
That's a friend. Falafel or the film first?
Falafel. Avi's been watching us since you came.
He's pretending to clean the same spot.
Third time. It's very clean.
Two in a pita, Avi. Extra pickles for the nervous one.

commentary.say: Hair down. No apron. Ishai's brain just left the building.
Noa briefed both sides. That's not a date, that's a summit.

moments.text: They eat standing at the counter, tahini on their fingers. Avi slides a little dish of extra pickles toward them without a word and goes back to the fryer.

lines.say: Sorry, you have tahini... there.
Three. And thank you. Here?
Other side. Sorry.
Four. It's eighteen thirty-five.
Okay. I'm asking a real question now.
Oh no. Noa's rule one.
Why basil? On my cup. Every day.
You told your cup to have a nice day. Once.
I don't remember that.
I do. Nobody talks to the cup.
Is that weird?
It's the nicest weird thing on Herzl Street.
Sorry. I'm just... happy.
Five. That one I'll allow.
Avi gave us pickles without a proverb.
He hasn't said a proverb in a week. Have you noticed?

commentary.say: Avi gave free pickles without a proverb. Something is very wrong at that kiosk.
'The nicest weird thing on Herzl Street.' Put it on a mug. Put it on my grave.

moments.text: They walk west along Herzl Street toward the park, the kiosk's light behind them. Dana walks a little closer than she needs to.

lines.say: So. The park, then the cinema. You planned it.
Noa planned it. I approved it.
Do you always let people plan for you?
Gadi plans my weekends. Noa plans my love life.
And who plans Ishai?
Moshe. Basically. He's very demanding.
How is he?
New leaf on Thursday. I'll send a photo.
You'll send it a week late.
Sorry.
Six.
That wasn't a real one.
They're all real, Ishai. That's the problem.
Is it a problem?
Ask me in the park.

commentary.say: 'Who plans Ishai?' She is asking the right questions, people.
Six sorries. One basil. Zero plans of his own.

beats.goal: Evening walk around the dark pond before the film. Ishai asks Zelig's question: where is she, tonight? She almost tells him: 'If someone offered you something... somewhere else...' and her phone rings, a 04 number. She declines it, says 'after the film', and changes the subject to the film. Ishai notices and doesn't push. They head off toward The Big S for the 21:00 film.
beats.teaser: In the park Dana starts a sentence. Her phone finishes it.
beats.forceText: In the dark park Dana almost tells Ishai something; a 04 number rings and she says 'after the film'.

forceLines.say: If someone offered you something... somewhere else...

forceCommentary.say: SHE WAS ABOUT TO SAY IT. Zero-four, I will find you.
Saved by the bell. Or ruined. Same bell.

moments.text: The park after dark: lamps on the path, the duck asleep on the pond. Dana and Ishai walk slowly; a cat watches them from a bench.

lines.say: Can I ask a question I got from a man who talks to pigeons?
Mr. Zelig. He told me I look at my phone like the sea.
He told me that too.
Great. The pigeon man gossips.
His question. Where are you? Tonight. Not in a year.
That's a good question. Annoyingly good.
You don't have to answer.
I'm here. Mostly here.
Mostly?
Seventy percent. Thirty is thinking.
About what?
Ishai... if someone offered you something.
Like what?
Something good. Somewhere else. Would you—

commentary.say: Zelig's question. Seventy percent here. That's an honest woman.
Somewhere ELSE? Don't stop there, Dana. Don't you dare stop there.

moments.text: Dana's phone rings in her coat pocket. She looks at the screen, a number starting 04, presses decline and puts it away. The duck wakes up and paddles off.

lines.say: Sorry. Ha. Now I'm doing it.
That's one for you. Who was it?
Nobody. A number.
The same number. Zero-four. Friday too.
You notice things.
I'm a designer. I notice kerning and phones.
After the film. I'll tell you after the film.
Okay. No questions.
That's it? Okay?
I'm practising. Someone taught me okay is enough.
It's a horror film. Will you scream?
Quietly. And apologise to the screen.
We should walk. The Big S is far.
Twenty minutes along the sea. I checked. Twice.
Of course you did.

commentary.say: She said sorry first! Score: Ishai six, Dana one. Love is a contact sport.
'After the film.' Doctor Moreau just became the second scariest thing tonight.

update.memory: First date: falafel at Avi's, six sorries, a walk in the park. Almost told him; the 04 number called. Said after the film.

beats.goal: After the film they come back to Herzl Street (a taxi along the sea). Under the street lamp by his building's door they talk about the film. Ishai reminds her gently: after the film. She says not tonight: tonight was too nice; Wednesday, after his Pump House night, she will tell him properly. A kiss on the cheek; she walks the last two streets home. He goes up alone. Hook: what is Wednesday?
beats.teaser: After the film: what Dana promised to tell him. Or not.
beats.forceText: Back on Herzl Street Dana says 'not tonight, Wednesday', kisses Ishai's cheek and walks home.

forceLines.say: Not tonight. Tonight was too nice. Wednesday.

forceCommentary.say: Cheek kiss! CHEEK KISS! I need a minute.
Wednesday. She just booked her own cliffhanger.

moments.text: Late on Herzl Street, quiet, the kiosk shuttered. Dana and Ishai stop under the street lamp by his building's door, both still a little jumpy from the film.

lines.say: The man with the dog face. I'll dream about him.
You grabbed my arm. Twice.
Once. The second time was the armrest.
The armrest was my arm.
Then it was a very soft armrest.
Eleven, by the way.
Eleven what?
Sorries. I counted after the falafel. Eleven.
You counted yourself? That's progress.
It was after the film. You said.
I said.
You don't have to. No questions.
Stop being nice, it makes it harder.
Makes what harder?

commentary.say: Eleven sorries, counted by the man himself. Growth comes in odd shapes.
'Stop being nice.' Dana, he physically cannot.

moments.text: Dana looks down the empty street, then back at him. She steps in and kisses his cheek, quick, and steps back, hands deep in her coat.

lines.say: Not tonight. Tonight was too nice to spend on it.
Is it bad?
It's not bad. It's... big. Wednesday.
Wednesday?
After your Pump House thing. Come by the café. I'll tell you properly.
Okay. Wednesday.
You're not going to ask?
I want to. I'm not going to.
Yael's class is dangerous.
Can I walk you home?
Two streets. I'm a big girl. Go up, Moshe is waiting.
Good night, Dana.
Good night, Ishai. Zero sorries in that one.
I noticed.

commentary.say: Cheek kiss. Under a street lamp. I'm calling it: season highlight.
'Wednesday.' Four days. In this building four days is a lifetime.

update.memory: First date with Ishai: falafel, the park, Doctor Moreau, eleven sorries he counted himself. Kissed his cheek. Promised to tell him Wednesday at the café.

moments.text: Ishai climbs the dim stairs to his door slowly, touching his cheek without noticing he's doing it.

lines.say: Wednesday. Something big. Not bad. Big.
Zero-four. Where is zero-four?

commentary.say: Zero-four is the north, Ishai. We all have maps.
He's touching his cheek. I'm not crying, you're crying.

hook.text: Dana kissed his cheek and promised to tell him on Wednesday at the café. 'Not bad. Big.' What is big, and who gets there first?

previously.text: Nobody talked. Noa came back from the stairs red-eyed, 'plumbers, the landlord, whatever'. He made honey tea, gave her the good blanket and asked nothing.

hosts: Saturday. Shabbat. The one day Gadi's emails feel guilty.
Noa folded a blanket. In eleven years of friendship, a first.
Three nights on an armchair. That's not a sleepover, that's a lease.
Today's forecast: clear skies, cool evening, one first date.
Shabbat goes out at 17:17. Ishai's nerves came in at 09:20.
Falafel versus the park pigeons. A rivalry for the ages.
Mr. Zelig has advice. Mr. Zelig always has advice. Today it's good.
Tomer bets on everything. Today he bets on Eilat. Bold.
The nap is at two. Even nerves need a nap.
18:30 at Avi's. Falafel as a first date. A classic of the genre.
Noa told him to count his sorries. Noa is a scientist now.
Jacket, not hoodie. The hoodie has soup on it. Facts.
Mrs. Levi wants her camera fixed. She also wants lipstick for it.
Moti promised to come after Shabbat. Moti promises a lot.
Tonight at the PixelPlex: The Island of Doctor Moreau. Horror. For a first date. Brave.
A horror film on a first date is a classic move. Somebody grabs an arm.
Avi hasn't said a proverb in a week. Somebody check on Avi.
Dana with her hair down. Herzl Street is not ready.
Ishai has a question ready. One. He rehearsed it on Falafel.
The duck in the pond has seen many first dates. The duck is unimpressed.
The walk to The Big S is twenty minutes along the sea. Twenty minutes of talking. Gulp.
Moshe the basil stays home tonight. Someone has to guard the apartment.
Monday is poker at Boaz's. Fifty to buy in. Small notes.
Gadi says Sunday. Tomorrow is Sunday. We'll see what Sunday means.
Lecture tomorrow at eleven: part two of the fake country man.
Every sorry tonight is a point for Noa's spreadsheet.
A Saturday with no market and no buses until evening. Tel Aviv, holding its breath.
Shavua tov, everybody. A good week starts with falafel.
radio: Radio Herzl 88.2, Saturday evening. Shavua tov to everyone just switching back on.
Shabbat is out at 17:17 in Tel Aviv. The buses are waking up, slowly, like us.
Clear skies tonight, fifteen degrees by the sea. Bring a coat, look romantic.
A listener asks: is falafel a date? Habibi, falafel is a commitment.
Tonight's request line: songs for people who are early and pretending they're not.
Traffic: everybody going back from their mother's at the same time. Again.
Fun fact: the Mediterranean is very calm tonight. Unlike some of you.
Reminder: the market opens tomorrow at seven. The tomatoes are rested.
Our next song goes out to a man in Toronto who should call his mother. Any man. Any mother.
If you're going to the movies tonight: phones off. We mean it. We'll know.
A caller says her cat watches the news. We believe her.
Herzl Street is quiet tonight. Quiet streets are where things begin.

zelig: The pigeons rest on Shabbat. Look at them. Lazy.
Not this sea. I keep saying it. Nobody writes it down.
Young people ask the future. Ask the bread.
michal: Rest days are for people who don't have mirrors.
One more set. Shabbat shalom, biceps.
sivan: Saturday pace. Still faster than the guy with the hascii.
Eight kilometres. Shavua tov to me.
He's on a date tonight. His pace will suffer.
lior: Chapter fifteen. She goes to the cinema.
The man counts his sorries. Keep that. Keep that.
Don't write the ending yet. Don't.
kobi: Saturday night numbers. Seven, seventeen, Shabbat out at seventeen-seventeen. A sign!
First drink after Shabbat tastes like a winner.
The apologiser has a date. I heard. Everybody heard.
One more and then I'm going home. I always say that.

street: ...shavua tov, did you see who's at the kiosk with the barista...
...no, the 88 starts again at six, sit down...
...my mother says the movies are for teenagers, I said I'm forty-one...
...is Avi okay? He gave me change without a proverb...
market: ...closed, closed, it's Saturday, what did you expect...
park: ...he walks the dog, the dog walks him, it's Shabbat, nobody's walking anybody...
...the old man was talking to the pigeons about 1971 again...
...that couple by the pond, first date, you can tell from the gap...
...the duck has a new spot, look, by the reeds...
cafe: ...one cappuccino and a croissant, it's Saturday, I'm allowed...
...the writer guy is still here, does he live here...
...she's not working tonight, she said she had plans, PLANS...

chat.say: Shavua tov. Reminder: recycling bins moved to the back. The front is for bicycles.
The camera works. Thank you Ishai. Moti, you are excused.
Excused from what? I was coming at 7.
Poker Monday 20:00. Bring small notes. Moti, bring your own pizza money.
Thank you all for a quiet Shabbat. The baby slept. A miracle.
Who came up the stairs singing? Never mind. I know who.
